property_summary: The fallback function must always require msg.value == 10 ether; the mutant allows calls with any value, which can cause the contract balance to change differently than the reference when a transfer is triggered.

For any call to the fallback with any msg.value, the reference either reverts (if msg.value != 10 ether) or proceeds; the mutant allows non-10 ether calls, which can result in a different contract balance when block.number % 15 == 0 and a full balance transfer occurs.

For any call to the fallback, the contract balance after the call must equal the balance before the call plus msg.value, unless the call reverts; the mutant can change the balance differently because it accepts calls with msg.value != 10 ether that do not revert.

After any external call to the fallback function, the contract's balance must equal msg.value if the call did not revert and block.number % 15 != 0; the buggy mutant violates this because it accepts calls with msg.value != 10 ether, transferring the full balance (which now includes the non-10 ether deposit) when block.number % 15 == 0.
For any call to fallback with msg.value != 10 ether, the call must revert in the reference contract; the mutant allows it to succeed, leading to a different contract balance when a transfer occurs.

Multiple fallback calls within the same block cannot all succeed transfers; the reference C allows at most one call per block, while the mutant M allows multiple calls until the balance is drained, causing a transfer revert after the balance drops below 10 ether.

In the reference contract, a successful fallback call always strictly advances pastBlockTime and never triggers a second transfer within the same block; the mutant allows a second call in the same block to succeed and transfer the balance again, leaving the contract balance less than the required 10 ether precondition for the first call.

For any admissible input (msg.value == 10 ether, timestamp strictly greater than pastBlockTime), a successful fallback call always sets pastBlockTime equal to block.timestamp. The mutant M breaks this because it allows a call with a timestamp equal to pastBlockTime (when block.timestamp == pastBlockTime), which leaves pastBlockTime unchanged.

In the reference contract, pastBlockTime is always strictly less than the current block.timestamp after any successful call; the mutant allows a successful call when block.timestamp == pastBlockTime, leaving pastBlockTime unchanged.
For any call that satisfies the requires, the contract balance becomes zero if and only if block.number is divisible by 15, but mutant zeroes the balance when block.number is NOT divisible by 15.

After any admissible sequence, the contract's balance must be zero, because the reference version always transfers the entire balance when block.number % 15 == 0 after a fixed deposit of 10 ether; the mutant never transfers, so balance accumulates to >0 and the invariant breaks.

The reference contract never transfers its entire balance on a block where block.number % 15 != 0, but after a successful fallback call the buggy contract can do so when block.number % 7 == 0 and block.number % 15 != 0.
